raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary Part of #53452. Adds Rust client-side support for EngineCore **streaming-input** sessions in two layers: 1. **`vllm-engine-core-client`** — resumable session lifecycle (state machine, `call_continuation`, client-side segment accounting mirroring Python `input_chunk_queue`). 2. **`vllm-llm`** — public facade: `Llm::generate_streaming`, `SegmentSink`, `GenerateRequest::resumable` / `sentinel()`. A resumable session stays open across segment `STOP`s and closes only after: 1. the final continuation ADD (`resumable: false`) is committed, and 2. every submitted segment has been reconciled with its engine stop. This PR does not expose `/v1/realtime`, WebSocket transport, or audio preprocessing. Relates to #44280. ## Session flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Caller participant Facade as Llm and SegmentSink participant Client as EngineCoreClient participant Engine Caller->>Facade: Llm::generate_streaming(first_segment) Facade->>Client: EngineCoreClient::call(resumable request) Client->>Engine: ADD first segment Facade-->>Caller: SegmentSink and one output stream loop Each additional segment Caller->>Facade: SegmentSink::push(segment) Facade->>Client: EngineCoreClient::call_continuation(content) Client->>Engine: ADD using the same request ID Engine-->>Client: Segment output and STOP Client-->>Caller: Output continues on the original stream end Caller->>Facade: SegmentSink::finish() Facade->>Client: EngineCoreClient::call_continuation(final sentinel) Client->>Engine: Final ADD with resumable false Engine-->>Client: Remaining segment STOPs Client-->>Caller: SessionFinished after every segment stops Note over Client,Caller: Each output is delivered before its STOP is reconciled Note over Client,Engine: Abort or error retires the session and cleans up engine state ``` A failed continuation send rolls back its in-flight accounting. If the session is retired after an ADD reaches the wire but before commit, commit reports the race and dispatches a detached ABORT so the engine cannot retain orphaned resumable state. ## Resumable session state machine ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR state "Open
final_sent=false" as Open state "Closing
final_sent=true ∧ outstanding>0" as Closing state "Finished
final_sent=true ∧ outstanding=0" as Finished state "Retired
Abort/Error STOP" as Retired [*] --> Open: call(resumable=true)
outstanding=1 Open --> Open: push → outstanding++
STOP → outstanding-- Open --> Closing: sentinel committed
(final_sent=true, outstanding>0) Open --> Finished: sentinel committed
(outstanding already 0) Closing --> Closing: STOP → outstanding-- Closing --> Finished: last STOP
(outstanding=0) Open --> Retired: Abort/Error STOP Closing --> Retired: Abort/Error STOP Finished --> [*] Retired --> [*] ``` Diagram states map to `ResumableSession` fields `final_sent` and `outstanding`. `Open` accepts more segments (`final_sent == false`). `Closing` means the sentinel ADD is committed (`final_sent == true`) while `outstanding > 0`. `Finished` is `final_sent && outstanding == 0`. The client enqueues each STOP output before reconciling it, and `Retired` covers abort or error stops. ### Key changes — engine-core-client - Add `call_continuation()` so one resumable `request_id` can receive multiple ADDs; close with `resumable: false`. - Keep the session registered across segment `STOP`s; close only after the final ADD is committed and every segment has stopped (client-side counting, mirroring Python `input_chunk_queue`). - Signal completion explicitly via `StreamEvent::SessionFinished` instead of relying on channel close. - Defer segment-stop reconciliation until after the output is enqueued, so a concurrent final commit cannot close the stream ahead of an already-routed output. - Abort leftover engine state whenever a continuation commit races with session retirement. The ADD is already on the wire; landing after the abort would have the engine admit it as a fresh resumable request that nothing would ever continue or free, leaving it parked in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` holding its KV blocks and a request slot. - Dispatch that cleanup abort from a detached task. `run_output_dispatcher_loop` is the single task fanning outputs out to every request stream, so it must not await a wire send. ### Key changes — llm facade - Thread `GenerateRequest::resumable` through `prepare()` to the wire. - Add `Llm::generate_streaming()` returning `(SegmentSink, GenerateOutputStream)`. - Add `SegmentSink::{push, finish}` wrapping `call_continuation`. `push` rejects a segment with `resumable: false`: engine-core reads that flag as the closing ADD, so it would end the session and discard the segment's own prompt. - Add `GenerateRequest::sentinel()` for the closing ADD (Python `final_req`). - `vllm-text` lowers every text request with `resumable: false`, leaving one-shot requests unchanged. This is the only change outside the two crates above and is required because `GenerateRequest` gained a field. ## Why this is not a duplicate Checked with: ```bash gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "53452 in:body" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "resumable streaming input" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "engine-core-client" ``` No other open PR references #53452. The open PRs in the streaming-input area — including #53861, #53321, #52765, #52717 and #55162 — all work on the Python engine and scheduler (`vllm/v1/core/sched/`, `vllm/v1/engine/`) and touch no files under `rust/`. This PR is entirely client-side in Rust and changes no engine behaviour. Other open PRs do touch `vllm-engine-core-client` (for example #54144 pooling support, #56533 output-field compatibility), but none of them covers resumable session lifecycle or segment accounting, so there is no overlapping change. ## Test plan Run from `rust/`: ```bash cargo check --workspace --all-targets cargo nextest run -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo fmt --all -- --check ``` Results: | Command | Result | | --- | --- | | `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` | clean | | `cargo nextest run -p vllm-engine-core-client` | 139 passed | | `cargo nextest run -p vllm-llm` | 26 passed | | `cargo nextest run -p vllm-text` | 92 passed, 1 skipped | | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean | | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean | | `pre-commit run --files ` | all hooks passed | The commands are workspace-scoped on purpose: `GenerateRequest` gains a field, which is a breaking change for every crate that builds one, so a crate-scoped run would not prove the tree still compiles. New tests covering the behaviour this PR adds: - `resumable_session_closes_on_the_last_stop_after_the_final_segment` and `resumable_session_closes_when_the_final_segment_follows_the_last_stop` — the two orderings of "final ADD" against "last segment STOP". - `resumable_session_aborts_leftover_engine_state_on_an_unresumable_stop` — a stop the session cannot resume from retires it client-side, so the engine has to be told to drop the request. - `resumable_session_abort_races_with_continuation` and `commit_reports_a_session_retired_by_abort` — commit racing with retirement. - `completion_does_not_overtake_an_already_routed_output` — the deferred reconciliation ordering guarantee. - `push_rejects_a_segment_that_would_close_the_session` — the `SegmentSink` guard, which must hold in release builds. - A state-machine transition suite over the `ResumableSession` phases. ## Model evaluation Not applicable: no model-output path changes. This PR is confined to the Rust frontend client. The only edit outside the two new-feature crates sets `resumable: false` on the existing text lowering path, which preserves current behaviour exactly, and no engine, scheduler, or sampling code is touched. ## Follow-ups (out of scope) - Sample-native audio preprocessing - WebSocket upgrade lifecycle - Qwen3-ASR `/v1/realtime` route ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for implementation exploration, code review, test scaffolding, and PR description drafting. The commands listed above were run locally on this branch. All changes were reviewed by the human submitter, who takes responsibility for them.
